piece_title: Regions, borders and the strange — round 1 critique

build.note: Working tree dirty (5 files) throughout, and being rewritten by ~20 concurrent pieces. Load 14.8-22.8 and 24-36 headless_shell processes for the whole run, far above RULES.md rule 21's ~8 cap, so I launched NO browser and took every number from node processes over files on disk. No timing figure is reported anywhere in this verdict, so contention affects nothing in it. The W1-02 builder was mid round-3 during my run: its blind-pack process (pid 3888) was capturing when I started and died at 20:59:22 after 24 of 48 frames. HEAD moved 6b1a142 -> e06f551 during the run: another agent's blanket add-and-commit swept this verdict, its json, both images, the blog line and my status file into that agent's commit. I ran git commit at no point. Every number is stamped to 6b1a142 and I re-ran the headline M65 measurement at e06f551 immediately before finishing - stddev 16.49/22.82/62.03, zero automatic fails, unchanged - and ANSWERS.json still hashes to be6fe0e2...

bifurcation.note: This piece is judged on structure and measurement, not on fidelity or art direction. The one image-based check, RI-WLD12 M68, is a PERCEPTUAL question about whether a border is legible ('is this one place or two?'), not a fidelity or art-direction comparison, and is scored on its own bars rather than on a bifurcated visual axis. INDEPENDENTLY REPLICATED. My own scorer over the shipped BorderField.traverse: 24/24 borders measurable, stddev(c) min 16.49 / median 22.82 / max 62.03 m, span 54-214 m, ZERO automatic fails (stddev<5m), zero failures of the per-kind stddev bar (25 m marked / 8 m hard), zero span failures, zero violations of the 3 m pair rule, one partial (marauders-coast--western-rootlands, 6/9 axes). All 7 jumps with |dtier|>=2 declare two channels (threshold_object + remains), and 110 objects stand on those borders. But T1 is scored off the DECLARED announcement.channels array that build-borders.mjs wrote, not off the world, and the item's 'within 100 m of the crossing' clause is never checked by any tool.

UNMEASURED. T3 (nothing gates the crossing — no level check, soft wall or scaled enemy) is one of RI-WLD12's AUTOMATIC FAILS and no tool in the repo measures it. T4 (sightline >=100 m into the far region) and T5 (>=3 borders descending in tier) likewise.
UNMEASURED, weight 14. grep of tools/ finds no instrument for M67, C2's 150 m streaming-vs-visual separation or C4's 80 m grade interpolation.

52.6% answered 'two' (10 of 19 usable frames) against a >=80% bar; the >=25%-answer-'one' fail clause FIRES at 47.4%. The cue bar PASSES: 80% of 'two' answers named an object or a landform, and the most common cue is a built object (6 of 10) with ZERO frames decided by fog or colour — RI-WLD12's 'fog border' failure mode does not occur. Pack shipped 24 of 48 frames.

16 of 24 frames have a foreground boulder within metres of the lens; 5 are unreadable. Two-rate is 75.0% on the 8 unoccluded frames and 36.4% on the 11 usable occluded ones. The camera pose is computed from node with no occlusion test, and the province scatters props in the renderer from noise. MARKED borders read 'two' 50% of the time, no better than HARD at 54.5%.
UNMEASURED, weight 6. No instrument.
The declared ambient bed differs across borders and the thirteen regions do not share one bed.

NONE of RI-WLD12's six 'Automatic fail regardless of score' conditions is triggered: no border has stddev(c)<5 m (min 16.49, replicated by me); no border lacks both a landform and an object (B2=0); no loading screen, fade or invisible wall was observed or reported; and fog/colour is the only cue on ZERO borders, against a threshold of 3 — in the whole blind pack not one frame was decided by a grade. The unmeasured one is the level-check/soft-wall/scaled-enemy condition (T3), recorded as a hole rather than as a pass. M68 missing its 80% bar costs the item its 16 points but is NOT on the automatic-fail list.

environment.js emits day_phase (:153) and weather_change (:197). Neither was in game/src/sim/events.js's closed vocabulary when this piece shipped them, and Environment.step() runs FIRST in stepOnce(), so every stepping probe in the project died on the frame the clock rolled while boot-check stayed green. NOW FIXED: my probe steps 300,000 frames clean (4 day_phase, 1 weather_change, no throw), and deleting the two entries throws on the first roll. The repair is commit dcf1d36 by W1-SOULS, NOT by W1-02, and W1-02's status file records none of it across 50 findings.

blind_comparisons.question: For each unlabeled frame: is this one place, or two? If two, what told you?
blind_comparisons.blind_rationale: blind_pick is 'none' because RI-WLD12 M68 is not an A/B design — there is no 'ours vs reference' side to pick, only a distribution of per-frame answers against the item's own bars. The result: 10 'two', 9 'one', 5 unusable over 24 frames = 52.6% 'two' on usable frames against an 80% bar, with the >=25%-'one' fail clause firing at 47.4%; cues were 6 object, 2 landform, 2 flora and ZERO colour or fog. Procedure pre-registered and hashed before any frame was opened. Verdict per frame required a spatially localised discontinuity — two different ground materials meeting, two plant populations, a built object on a line, a landform edge. Free-text cue written first, classified afterwards from the noun written first, with flora resolved strictly AGAINST us because M68's pass clause names only an object or a landform. 5 frames declared unusable rather than guessed. Answers hashed before the key was derived; the builder's KEY.json never existed because its process died at 24 of 48 frames.

ar2.note: Seam S35 makes region identity MORE load-bearing, not less: the map shows only travelled terrain, so it cannot tell a player where they are going. The piece is aligned with that — it invests in borders and threshold objects rather than in markers, and M68's cue result (zero frames decided by colour, six by a built object) is the AR-2-positive finding: where the world announces a boundary it does so with a thing, not a HUD element.

Against those: RI-WLD12 M65, the weight-30 core check, is genuinely solid and I replicated it independently with a working sabotage control; the clock is correct to RI-WLD08 §1's exact numbers and is consumed by five systems; M19's ONLY-HERE audit passes cleanly.

biggest_gap.what: The RI-WLD12 M68 blind pack cannot answer the question it exists to ask, because the camera is standing inside the scenery. Of 24 frames shipped, 16 have a foreground boulder within a few metres of the lens and 5 are unreadable; I answered 'two places' on 52.6% of usable frames against an 80% bar, and the >=25%-'one' fail clause fired at 47.4%. Stratified by whether the lens was blocked, the two-rate is 75.0% on the 8 unoccluded frames and 36.4% on the 11 usable occluded ones. The pose is computed in node at the crossover coordinate with no occlusion test, and the province scatters its props in the renderer from noise, so nothing on the node side knows what is in front of the lens. The pack is also half-built — the builder's process died at 24 of 48 frames, so KEY.json and QUESTION.md were never written — and the frames are 1280x720 where M68 specifies 1920x1080.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: This is the check that decides whether the piece's headline bar is met at all, and seam S35 raised its stakes: the map now shows only terrain already travelled, so it cannot tell a player where they are going, and region identity has to carry that load alone. The measurement currently cannot be cited in either direction — it is not evidence that the borders fail, and it is not evidence that they work. Worse, the builder itself wrote the warning that predicts this exactly in its round-2 handover — 'at a border the flora is dense BY CONSTRUCTION, and nothing on the node side knows what is between the lens and the subject, since the scatter happens in the renderer from noise' — after losing two frames to it, and then built the pack tool without carrying that lesson into it. The same lesson was lost twice inside one piece. The positive half of the result should not be lost either: where a border IS visible, zero frames were decided by fog or colour and six of ten by a built object, so RI-WLD12's 'fog border' failure mode and S24's 'a region only distinguishable by fog colour is a defect' do not occur anywhere in this pack.

Shoot at 1920x1080 as M68 specifies, complete all 48 frames, write KEY.json into a sibling wld12-blind.reveal/ directory rather than inside the pack, and remove the scoring rule from QUESTION.md so the judge is not told which cue loses.
remedy.acceptance: 48 frames at 1920x1080, no more than 4 of them with geometry inside 4 m of the lens; KEY.json outside the pack directory; QUESTION.md silent on scoring; and a fresh judge who did not build the pack answers >=80% 'two' with >=70% naming an object or a landform. Re-running the same judgement on the CURRENT 24 frames must still reproduce 52.6%, so the change is demonstrably the camera and not the scoring.

Two of eight threshold-object types are the colour of the ground they stand on, measured against ground.albedo on RI-WLD04 M18's own dE>12 yardstick: imperial_border_cairn dE 4.2 on Valus Ridge, corpse_in_a_cage dE 10.8 on Blackwood. The builder's distinctness proof was explicitly 'colour-free, size-free' and structurally could not catch this. salt_glass_marker is also the shortest of the twelve types at a median 1.11 m against root_gate's 4.27 m.

RI-WLD04 M18's weather axis is still listed in reports/region-axes.json dropped_axes with the reason 'weather is a per-frame capture parameter, not a property of the built world'. W1-02 falsified that by shipping 13 per-region state machines and did not re-arm the instrument.

RI-TRV01's day/night gate is prose: 'night: the roots close 20:00-05:00' sits in game/data/world/travel/services.json:36 and no travel code reads a clock. The item N-fails on 'every mode available always, at any hour, in any weather'. A seam between W1-02 and W1-05 that neither has claimed.

CORPUS HOLE: three of the ten items docs/PLAN.md §3 names as W1-02's judges bind only by legacy path alias — RI-WLD04 judges world.regions/world.weather, RI-WLD05 judges world.strangeness/world.architecture, RI-PRG04 judges world.time. Assembled by me from every judges: line in corpus/*/RI-*.md. RI-WLD04 is the item that owns the phrase 'thirteen regions distinguishable without the map' and by front-matter it does not judge this piece. CORPUS-CONTRACT §4 rule 2 amendment recommended.

The builder's status file twice describes its own blind pack as asking 'whether a stranger can NAME the object at a border'. That is a provenance-shaped question where the item specifies a perceptual one — the exact error that voided a third comparison in this project. The TOOL does not make that mistake: QUESTION.md asks M68 verbatim. The prose is wrong and the artifact is right, and this is recorded in the builder's favour.

CREDIT WHERE DUE. This piece found three consumption failures by measurement and fixed them; found a real cross-system defect nobody had noticed (stealth classifying only 3 of 20 weather ids, lighting salt-storms as midday sun while the renderer drew a black sky); found a live bug by READING the release path that no probe would have caught, then wrote the probe that catches it; self-caught three probe defects including one where a check took its scope from the table it was testing and passed 8/8 against a build where nothing was solid; and declared M66 T3 failing rather than editing another piece's data mid-session.

gap_closure.note: The prior round's finding that 8 of 9 RI-WLD04 axes were string comparisons against regions.json is closed: region-axes.mjs was rewritten to measure the built world, drops unmeasurable axes explicitly rather than scoring them 78/78, and now reports min_axes_differing 10 against a bar of 9. Not W1-02's work, but verified standing at this commit.

The prior round's pack shipped in declaration order and 39 of 39 answers came off the file index. This pack is a genuine deterministic Fisher-Yates shuffle on seed 0xb11d with opaque filenames; I verified the shuffle in the source and found no ordering signal. The builder also did not judge its own pack.

field.regionAt was a bare raster read, so all nine RI-WLD04 axes crossed at exactly one coordinate and stddev(c) was 0 by construction on all 24 borders — RI-WLD12's named automatic fail. Now 16.49-62.03 m with zero automatic fails, independently replicated by me, with a sabotage control that reproduces the old state exactly.

217 threshold markers were coordinates that nothing drew or collided with. Now 12 instanced silhouettes, solid at the collision frame, with a browser probe at 6/6 including a 2.4 km round trip that catches the shared-geometry release bug.
sim.env.timeOfDay was initialised to 12.0 and advanced only by harness verbs. The fixed step now advances it and five systems change behaviour.
5 of 7 announced tier jumps violated, worst 0.69 m against a declared 40 m. Measured, named and handed over by the builder; the fix belongs to whoever owns population-posts.json.

fog.height_falloff_m is declared 45-340 m per region and read by nobody; render/sky.js uses FogExp2, which has no height term. W1-01-r4 measured the vertical luminance profile as the only half of the colour-stripped descriptor carrying signal, so this remains the highest-value unbuilt region-identity lever. Carried forward from round 1 untouched.

corpus_extended.what: An internal contradiction in RI-WLD12 §1's border taxonomy as built.
corpus_extended.detail: §1's table gives MARKED a 60-120 m transition width; the province ships all 10 MARKED borders at 123-172 m and zero GRADED borders. B3 bars only the GRADED width, so with no GRADED borders in existence B3 is vacuous and the MARKED width has no bar enforcing it. A builder can therefore satisfy every numbered bar while every border in the province is outside the table it was built from — which is what happened, and the builder's own status file scored the widths against the GRADED row.
